note: Conformance vectors for the Expenses entry format v1 (contracts/expenses/entry.v1.schema.json, ADR 0108 decisions 5 and 9, docs/apps/expenses.md § Entries and § What the client computes), so every client computes the same balance from the same entries. `conversion`: an entry's total into the base currency, round_half_away_from_zero(amount * rate * 10^(baseMinorUnits - minorUnits)). `rounding`: the largest-remainder allocation of an integer `total` by `weights` (exact fractions as strings), people in join order, `expected` per person in that order; its last two totals are the largest amount the schema takes, so every `total * weight` passes 2^53 and a floating-point division anywhere in the allocation gets one of them wrong. `pots`: whole Pots — participants, the current revision of each entry (the `body` minus `v` and `heads`, which carry no arithmetic), and per entry and per Pot what every client must compute, `settleUp` in the order the transfers are suggested. A Pot's `invalid`, where it has one, lists entries every client counts nowhere and shows as invalid, each with the reason (`problem`) this client names it by. Generated by an independent Python implementation (fractions.Fraction, decimal.Decimal) from the rules as the schema states them, which also re-checked `conversion` and `rounding`. The sections after `pots` pin every other rule a client answers alike, each case with its `rule`: `read` (a parsed body held to the schema: the body it reads to, or the `path` of the first rule it breaks), `decode` (the plaintext bytes, `utf8` or `hex`, where two JSON parsers could disagree: a duplicate key's last value wins, `1e2`, `100.0` and `-0` are integers, a byte order mark is dropped), `encode` (what a writer seals: its length in bytes and its JSON, whose key order carries no meaning), `check` (the ledger check, the current heads and the heads a write names, over held revisions whose `body` null did not open), `entryProblem`, `splitBreaks` and `named` (the unbalanced-entry rule), `ledger` (a whole Pot's state per record, its balances, settle-up and overviews; maps as `[key, value]` pairs in their order), `settleUp`, `amounts` (amounts as typed and shown, per language) and `rates` (the day's table and the cross rate). Their `expected` were first recorded from the web's TypeScript, which the core then answered case for case.

pots.name: trip
pots.note: Anna and Ben joined at the same millisecond, so their ids order them; Cleo joined a second later. Each entry's `expected` gives its total in the base currency, what each person paid (or received) and their share, in base minor units; `balances` is paid minus share summed over the entries (a transfer credits its giver and debits its receiver; a refund debits its receivers and credits its beneficiaries), positive = is owed. The entries pin each allocation rule: Dinner is all rest (no items, equal among everyone); Trattoria's rest of 7.01 goes by shares 2:1:1 with a remainder; Museum (yen) is all rest by shares, a tie of remainders broken by join order; the refund has two receivers and an item; Taxi is an exact amount per person (one item each, no rest, no rest split); Bar is items plus a tip shared equally; Groceries has two payers, an item by percent (33.33/33.33/33.34) and one by shares, each with a remainder; Ferry (pounds) has an item and a rest, so its base total is first allocated to the two parts with a remainder (23.45 and 15.63), and each part then among its people.

pots.name: settle-up
pots.note: The settle-up re-chooses the largest remaining debtor and the largest remaining creditor at every step (ties by join order). Walking two queues sorted once would answer Dee->Ada 10.000, Dee->Bo 3.000, Eli->Bo 5.000, Eli->Cy 7.000 instead; this case tells the two apart.

pots.name: amounts
pots.note: The `amounts` split mode: each person of a part a fixed amount in the entry's currency, summing to the part's amount, weighted by those amounts when the part's base amount is allocated. Ida and Jon joined at the same millisecond, Kai a second later. Hut (euro, the base) is all rest by amounts, so each person gets exactly their amount; Market (francs) is all rest by amounts 33.33/33.34/33.34 of a converted 95.13, whose cent left over goes to the largest cut-off remainder, Ida's, the smallest amount; Boat (yen) has an item by amounts and a rest shared equally, so its base total is first allocated to the two parts, then each part among its people. `invalid` holds entries that count nowhere and are shown as invalid, each with the reason this client names: amounts beside the rest's amount, an item's amounts beside the item's amount, and a person named twice in one split. `expected` counts the `entries` alone.
